stayOverview: Start with City centre for the easiest first Chicago stay, then compare Old Town and Waterfront when price, nightlife, quieter evenings or transfer timing matter more than being beside every major sight.
hotelIntro: Chicago hotel choice is mostly about repeat journeys: use City centre for sightseeing, Old Town for a different local base, and Waterfront or Airport area when views, parking, airport timing or longer stays matter.
rentalCars: Do not rent a car for central Chicago unless parking and traffic are part of the plan; use one mainly for regional day trips.

history.label: 1780s
history.text: Du Sable was of African descent, perhaps born in the French colony of Saint-Domingue (Haiti), and he established the settlement in the 1780s.
Army constructed Fort Dearborn, which was destroyed during the War of 1812 in the Battle of Fort Dearborn by the Potawatomi before being later rebuilt.
The Potawatomi were forcibly removed from their land after the 1833 Treaty of Chicago and sent west of the Mississippi River as part of the federal policy of Indian removal.
The City of Chicago was incorporated on Saturday, March 4, 1837, and for several decades was the world's fastest-growing city.
Chicago's first railway, Galena and Chicago Union Railroad, and the Illinois and Michigan Canal opened in 1848.

history.label: 1850s
history.text: The Chicago Board of Trade (established 1848) listed the first-ever standardized "exchange-traded" forward contracts, which were called futures contracts. 1850–1874 In the 1850s, Chicago gained national political prominence as the home of Senator Stephen.
Lincoln was nominated in Chicago for U.S. president at the 1860 Republican National Convention, which was held in a purpose-built auditorium called the Wigwam.
Rauch established a plan for Chicago's park system in 1866.
On October 8, 1871, the Great Chicago Fire destroyed an area about 4 miles (6.4 km) long and 1-mile (1.6 km) wide, a large section of the city at the time.
The University of Chicago, formerly at another location, moved to the same South Side location in 1892.
In 1900, the problem of sewage contamination was largely resolved when the city completed a major engineering feat.
In 1956, the city conducted its last major expansion when it annexed the land under O'Hare airport, including a small portion of DuPage County.

Major construction projects, including the Sears Tower (now known as the Willis Tower, which in 1974 became the world's tallest building), University of Illinois at Chicago, McCormick Place, and O'Hare International Airport, were undertaken.

history.label: Regional role
history.text: As the site of the Chicago Portage, the city became an important transportation hub between the eastern and western United States.
